=== (2) WHAT I CONCLUDED, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE ===

C1 — I2 PASS on both WZO2 artifacts. Evidence: my independent check (docs/evidence/BATTERY/i2-wzo2-T270/check_i2_wzo2.py, committed) on 4×4 0c3366f0 (0 violations / 0 not_found / 99,133,036 checked) and 3×3 d79c17cd (0 violations / 0 not_found / 49,428 checked). Two internal implementations (pure-Python dict pairing; vectorized composite-key searchsorted) agree exactly at 3×3 (full) and at the 4×4 low-colex 2M-group window (7,939,236 checked each, 58 not_found each — window-boundary artifacts, both impls identical).

C2 — The brief's premise 'I2 has never been run against WZO2' is STALE per the register. Evidence: SPRINT-M4a-ACCEPT row and m4a-accept-T212 stdout record A3 (which DIRECTION §7.1 equates to I2) on this exact artifact at 0/99,133,036. The T258 fleet run tested only the WZO1 list — that part of the premise is true — but M4a's instrument had already run the invariant on WZO2. I treated my run as the Phase-1 re-derivation of a registered claim with an independent instrument, which is the correct move either way, and recorded the premise discrepancy in the evidence doc and the finding's rationale.

C3 — The WZO2 artifact does NOT share the v1 basic-ko inversion defect (4x4.V1-INVSYM-BROKEN, ~11.66M violations ≈ 48%). Evidence: exhaustive I2 over every stored entry, zero violations. Consistent with T212 (0) and with T261's characterization of the artifact as internally consistent (A3/A4/A5/A6/A9 pass).

C4 — I2 is blind to CODE.WZO2-INCOMPLETE. Evidence: the certified-defective calibration input (missing ~6.77M passes=1 side-entries) passes I2 with not_found=0. I reasoned the missingness must be colour-symmetric (missing entries come in flip-pairs, so every present entry's inverse is present); the 0 not_found result is the empirical confirmation. Calibration conclusion: a battery expecting I2 to fail this known-bad input is wrong; the completeness-family checks (A1/A2/A8) carry that load.

C5 — Structural integrity of both artifacts is good: embedded SHA-256 (slot-zeroed) verifies, group index strictly sorted, L≤H on all 99,133,036 entries, score range within [−16,+16], passes≥1⇒ko=none invariant holds, unused key-byte bits zero. Evidence: the checker's diagnostics on both artifacts.

C6 — self_inverse_groups=1 at 4×4 is correct and is a flip-math sanity check: only the empty goban is colour-self-inverse (a non-empty position cannot map to itself under black↔white swap). Verified independently for layers 0-2 by brute force.

=== (3) WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===

E1 — I did not run the pure-Python reference implementation over the FULL 4×4 (99.1M entries; tens of minutes in Python). The numpy implementation is cross-validated against it at 3×3 (full) and the 4×4 low-colex window, and the full-4×4 numpy result matches T212's registered A3 numbers exactly. I judge the risk of a size-dependent divergence low, but the strongest possible form of the claim (both impls on the full 4×4) was not produced.

E2 — I could not verify the game-theoretic correctness of the values (L/H are only tested for the inversion identity, not for minimax correctness). I2 is a symmetry invariant; it says nothing about whether the scores are the true fresh-start brackets. That is outside the brief and remains the domain of Bellman-type checks (I4/A2), which were out of scope.

E3 — I did not check the 3×2 and 4×3 WZO2 artifacts (not on disk at dispatch) or any other WZO2 goban. Per-goban epistemic independence means my PASS at 3×3 and 4×4 is not evidence at other sizes.

E4 — I did not verify the exact colour-symmetry mechanism of the passes=1 incompleteness by direct side-by-side group inspection (e.g., counting groups where passes=1 exists for one side and confirming the flip-group has the complementary side). The 0 not_found across 99,133,036 checked entries is strong indirect evidence, but I never looked at a single example group's passes=1 layout directly.

=== (4) WHAT I ASSUMED WITHOUT CHECKING ===

A1 — That T212's A3 and my I2 are truly the same check. I read checkA3 and mirrored its semantics deliberately (masked key, first-match, terminal ignored, not_found counted separately), and both produce identical numbers on this artifact. But I did not diff my implementation against the Zig source line-by-line; a semantic difference that happens to agree on this artifact cannot be fully excluded.

A2 — That the embedded SHA-256 slot covers bytes 40..72 (40+32) zeroed, per the format spec §4.2. I verified the digest matches the stored slot on both real artifacts — if my zeroing window were wrong, the match would be a coincidence, so the empirical match validates the assumption on these files. For the synthetic fixtures the embedded hash is all-zeros and my checker reports embedded_sha256_ok=false; I did not make the fixture writer compute real hashes (not needed for the I2 path).

A3 — That numpy integer semantics (uint64 shifts, int8 negation) behave as I expect on this platform. The calibration fixtures and the agreement between the two implementations are the evidence that they do; I did not write explicit unit tests for e.g. -(-128) wraparound (irrelevant here since |L|≤16).

A4 — That 'first-match wins' in the artifact's lookup convention is what searchsorted(side='left') reproduces. This matters only if a group contains two entries with the same masked key (terminal variants); I did not check whether any such duplicate exists in the artifacts, and the 0-violation result would be insensitive to which match is chosen only if duplicate-masked-key groups have equal L/H or none exist.

A5 — That the runner's 4096 MB RSS cap would be sufficient for the full-4×4 numpy path. It was (peak 3897 MB) after two failed attempts that blew the cap (4546 MB, 4255 MB) and forced the chunked memory redesign. The first attempt's failure is the evidence I nearly got wrong.
